items.description:
As API
estates grow, managing individual custom domains and certificates for every
subdomain can quickly become operationally complex and difficult to
scale. Without wildcard support, every new subdomain — whether
payments.api.contoso.com, inventory.api.contoso.com, or orders.api.contoso.com
— requires its own hostname registration and certificate, meaning a team
onboarding ten new API surfaces generates ten separate domain and certificate
management tasks.  With
this update, Azure API Management Premium v2 and Standard v2 now support
wildcard entries in custom hostnames,  allowing a single
entry like *.api.contoso.com  and a single wildcard
certificate to cover all subdomains automatically — no per-subdomain
configuration required. This helps teams:  
 Simplify certificate and domain
     management at scale  
 Reduce operational overhead for
     rapidly growing API environments  
 Maintain consistent branded API
     endpoints across dynamic subdomains  
 Accelerate onboarding of new API
     surfaces without repeated hostname configuration  By
extending this capability to both Premium v2 and Standard v2, Azure API
Management makes flexible and scalable domain management accessible to more
organizations without requiring higher-tier deployments.  Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure API Management Premium v2 and Standard v2 now support wildcard custom hostnames.

Azure Policy now provides centralized governance for deployments using the model router. Organizations can define and enforce routing standards across their environment, helping ensure that model selection aligns with security, compliance, and operational requirements.
Built-in policy definitions allow teams to govern deployment regions, approved model lists, required routing rules, and logging configurations. Administrators can apply policies across management groups and subscriptions, identify deployments that drift from approved configurations, and remediate issues using existing Azure governance workflows.
Because the integration is built on Azure Policy’s native framework, customers can use familiar tools for compliance monitoring, exemptions, remediation, and reporting without additional engineering effort. items.description: Microsoft Foundry introduces rubric evaluators for measuring agent quality, now in public preview for single-turn and multi-turn agent flows. Rubric evaluators enable developers to define context-specific evaluation criteria using agent prompts, production traces and context-specific files with weighted dimensions and optional human review, ensuring that quality is measured against what truly matters for each scenario. This establishes a reliable baseline that is powering downstream workflows, including evaluation, optimization, regression testing and deployment gates.  Learn More

items.description: Azure AI Search now supports Content Understanding chunking and image verbalization in public preview, expanding the built-in skill that parses rich documents during indexing. Indexers can split documents into semantically meaningful chunks and generate text descriptions of embedded images, charts, and diagrams in the same pass. Retrieval-augmented generation apps benefit because each chunk carries the visual context that used to be lost when images were stripped out. Customers indexing slide decks, technical manuals, and scanned forms get higher answer quality without running a separate vision pipeline. The skill plugs into existing integrated vectorization workflows, so teams can add it to current skillsets without rebuilding indexes from scratch. This release ships under the same Azure AI Search billing and data residency commitments customers already use today. Learn more.

Clinical informatics teams and ISVs can paste discharge summaries, doctor's notes, or research abstracts and see extracted diagnoses, medications, symptoms, and time references with UMLS entity linking and relation extraction in a single view. The playground returns FHIR-structured output alongside the standard JSON response, so teams can validate downstream integration with electronic health record systems before writing a line of code. Supported input languages, entity categories, and assertion detection match the production service. The same Foundry resource powers both the playground and the REST API. Learn more.

Approved Custom Voice customers can now upload voice talent recordings and consent statements, run data quality checks, train neural voice models, and deploy to endpoints from the same Foundry project that hosts their text-to-speech, Speech-to-text, and Voice Live workloads.  They can also train Personal voice in Foundry. The experience replaces the previous Speech Studio Custom Voice flow with consistent Foundry navigation, role-based access, and project-scoped resources. Existing custom voice models, test scripts, and endpoints carry over without retraining. Custom Voice remains a Limited Access feature, so customers must already be approved through the intake form before they can use the portal. Learn more.

items.description: Microsoft Foundry observability introduces intelligent trace filtering and sampling for evaluations in public preview. Instead of running evaluations against all production traces, Foundry now select a representative subset of traces using a multi-stage MinHash farthest-first diversity algorithm, including deduplication, hard filers, aggregation and diversity-based selection for evaluation. This approach improves cost efficiency while producing significantly higher lexical diversity and diverse coverage compared to random sampling. Intelligent sampling is particularly effective for: evaluation and benchmarks, rubric generation and finetuning dataset curation.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Evaluations with Intelligent Trace Sampling

items.description: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service adds agent-to-agent (A2A) communication in public preview for Prompt agents and Hosted agents that use the responses protocol. Agents can call other agents by name through a managed endpoint, with identity, content safety, and audit logging applied to every hop. Developers can model multi-step business processes as a small set of cooperating agents instead of a single monolithic prompt, then trace the full conversation across agents in Application Insights. Because A2A is a first-class protocol in Agent Service, agents written with Agent Framework, LangGraph, or direct code can all participate in the same network without protocol shims. This release helps teams move from single-agent prototypes toward production multi-agent systems with the same enterprise controls already used for individual agents. Learn more.

items.description:
Azure Container Linux is a container-optimized, immutable operating system for
AKS node pools — derived from Flatcar Container Linux and built on Azure Linux
RPM packages. It delivers a locked-down, minimal host purpose-built for running
containerized workloads at scale. Key features include: Immutable by design — The root /usr directory is
read-only with dm-verity integrity verification. There is no package manager on
the host — what ships in the image is what runs in production. This eliminates
configuration drift and ensures consistent node state across your fleet. Container-optimized — Minimal OS footprint with
only the components needed to run Kubernetes workloads. Out-of-the-box security — SELinux in enforcing mode applies strict least-privilege policies to all processes. Trusted Launch with a Unified Kernel Image (UKI) verifies boot integrity from firmware through kernel, ensuring nodes haven't been tampered with before they join your cluster. Derived from Flatcar — Built on Flatcar Container Linux's proven architecture: declarative node configuration, systemd-first service management, and an operational model designed for fleets of immutable nodes. Built on Azure Linux — Powered by the Azure Linux RPM ecosystem with Microsoft's security patching cadence, CVE response SLAs, and integrated support through Azure. Learn more and get started:  Tech Community blog post Azure Container Linux Documentation Azure Linux Documentation Azure Linux on GitHub

items.description: In September 2023, we announced Azure Blueprints would retire on July 11, 2026. items.description:
AI pipelines for Azure HorizonDB is now
available in public preview. AI pipelines let you describe an AI data ingestion
workflow, chunking, embedding, extraction, generation, and ranking,
declaratively in SQL, and run it as a fault-tolerant pipeline inside the
database.  Execution is durable: pipelines survive crashes, retry failed steps
automatically, checkpoint incremental work, and resume long-running jobs from
the last completed step. This removes the boilerplate ingestion service that many GenAI
applications rebuild today. Pipelines run on change, so embeddings stay in sync
as source rows are inserted or updated, and only new or changed rows need to be
re-embedded. When the embedding model,
dimensions, or chunk size change, backfill reprocesses every row as a single
durable instance that resumes from the last checkpoint instead of restarting
from zero. AI pipelines are part of the azure_ai extension, built on pg_durable, and work with AI model management, pgvector,
DiskANN vector search, and full-text search to provide an end-to-end retrieval
path inside one database. Learn
more.

items.description: Application Gateway for Containers is extending its ingress gateway feature set with new AI gateway capabilities. The new inference gateway capability brings the Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension to Application Gateway for Containers, enabling load and model-aware routing for self-hosted generative AI workloads on AKS.Application Gateway for Containers' inference gateway capability is purpose-built for serving LLMs and other inference workloads, routing requests based on model server signals rather than generic load balancing — improving Time to First Token (TTFT) and reducing timeouts under load.Managed Body-Based Router (BBR): A fully managed router that inspects the request body (such as the model field on OpenAI-compatible APIs) to drive model-aware routing — no custom proxy tier required.Bring your own Endpoint Picker (EPP): Choose the EPP implementation that fits your workload to drive metrics-aware endpoint selection across your InferencePool.Secure inference: Pairs natively with the existing web application firewall (WAF) capability in Application Gateway for Containers, applying OWASP-aligned protections to AI traffic before it reaches your model servers.Improved performance and reliability: Routes around saturated replicas and leverages model server state to lower TTFT, reduce timeouts, and improve GPU utilization.Learn more:Application Gateway for Containers – AI gateway - Inference gatewayApplication Gateway for Containers - Overview
